mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has risen 4.6 points week-on-week (t-1w to t-0w: -32.9 to -28.3), signaling resumption of commuting. This sustained recovery in transit use over the next four weeks will drive increased retail footfall as workers return to shopping patterns adjacent to commute routes.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.6 points in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines by more than 3 points in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near -47.3% after volatile decline from -58.3%, indicating outdoor activity substitution is plateauing. As this substitution effect exhausts, suppressed retail demand will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stabilized at -47.3% in t-0w after -43.4% in t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises more than 10 points in any single week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 points from current baseline.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered 0.3 points week-on-week (t-1w to t-0w: -29.4 to -29.1) while RESIDENTIAL has declined 0.2 points, indicating marginal shift from home to workplace. If this trend accelerates over the next two weeks, retail recovery will follow within the subsequent two weeks as workplace-adjacent shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 2 points in any single week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility falls below -30% in any of the next two weeks, or RESIDENTIAL does not decline further, indicating no sustained shift from home to workplace.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has declined consistently from -12.0% to -14.6%, signaling tightening restrictions on non-essential retail or consumer avoidance of mixed-use venues. If this decline continues below -15% in the next week, RETAIL_REC will fall an additional 5+ points as consumers restrict discretionary shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined 0.6 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes or rises above -14.0% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not decline further.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 9.9% to 9.1% over four weeks, indicating sustained outflow from homes. Combined with TRANSIT recovery (t-0w: -28.3%), this dual signal of mobility resumption will drive retail recovery as consumers return to in-person shopping within the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 9.0% AND TRANSIT rises above -25%
failure_condition: Either RESIDENTIAL rises above 9.5% or TRANSIT falls below -30% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase from current baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined 11 points from t-3w to t-0w (-58.3% to -47.3%), indicating seasonal shift away from outdoor activity. This seasonal compression will redirect consumer time and spending toward indoor retail venues, producing a 3-5 point rise in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 11 points over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -40% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both improved in t-0w (WORKPLACES +0.3, TRANSIT +4.6), signaling coordinated return to commuting infrastructure. If both series improve simultaneously in the next week, retail recovery will accelerate within two weeks as workplace-commute-retail chains reactivate.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise more than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved in t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT declines in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not rise by at least 3 points within two weeks of the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -37.7% over the last week after declining from -38.1%, indicating floor effect. If GROCERY_PHARM continues declining (current trend: -12.0% to -14.6%), consumers will avoid all retail venues, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery and keeping it flat or lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above -15.0% or rises, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 points from current baseline over the next four weeks.
